BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter
Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of
Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.
SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)
Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims
is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same
caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.
Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and
non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public
registers (see Disclosure Letter).
Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the
Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or
public records.
Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller
will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the
counterparty's written consent.
Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding)
will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.
Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing
bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds
flow.)
Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio
matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.
Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter
and is not expected to be material.
Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course
operating costs.
Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime
above.
Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and
records are fictional.
1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including
DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly
searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific
disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,
payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.
2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause
11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final
written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.
3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security
is included.
4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of
every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of
non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject
to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft
Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or

email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity

person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation
remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no
loss amount.

a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.
8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each

each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale
consent is required merely because shares are sold.
10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of
the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the
Buyer has completed its own verification.
11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer
must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Scope note:** I'm working from the Seller's summary positions and disclosure letter, not the full SPA text. Drafting should be checked against the full mark-up before anything is sent. Nothing below is agreed, and the Seller's "key negotiated positions" label does not bind Wattlebridge.

## Part 1: Where the Seller departs from the playbook

### A. Liability architecture

| Issue | Seller draft | Our playbook | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m opening. 20% is a conditional fallback needing Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None given. | The Seller has written our fallback in as their position. |
| De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x higher. Small claims drop out. |
| Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess-only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | Five times the threshold, and we'd absorb the first AUD 250k of losses. |
| General claims period (cl 12.3) | 18 months | 24 months. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval. None given. | Fallback presented as settled. |
| Fundamental/Title | Subject to general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | This is the most serious structural departure. Title and capacity would be capped at AUD 4.8m and expire at 18 months. |
| Cross-application of limits (cl 12/13) | Limitations apply to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise" | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate. No hidden general-regime override. | Default-to-general drafting would pull every category into the general regime. |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance | No fraud carve-out. The Seller's wording would bar fraud claims. |

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

- **Schedule 7 / DL 1.1–1.2:** The Seller discloses the entire data room (as at 5pm 22 Sept 2026) and public registers. This is whole-data-room deemed disclosure, which the playbook rejects. Only specific, fair disclosure is acceptable.
- **Cl 8.3 (buyer knowledge):** Bars any claim where the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge," including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records." This is a blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion, which we delete. Any knowledge qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. As drafted, the clause would also defeat the specific indemnities we are seeking for Ironquay and the bonuses.

### C. Specific conditions and matters

- **Bluefen (cl 3/6.3; DL §2):** The Seller will use "reasonable endeavours" and treat consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's consent. The disclosure letter confirms no final written consent or evidence of satisfied conditions exists. The playbook requires an effective consent plus evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion, not consent-on-delivery, and reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material consent. Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (AUD 3.6m).
- **Riverlark (cl 2/7; DL §3):** The AUD 3.2m facility is to be released after Completion. The playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval. Neither is in the draft.
- **Funds flow (DL §5):** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are excluded from the draft funds flow, and the Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller." The playbook requires them as a specific line item or Seller-funded, with the triggered on-costs (payroll tax, super, etc.) also covered. The disclosure doesn't say whether on-costs apply, so the amount is unquantified.
- **Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL §4):** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and called "adequate." The playbook requires broadening it, keeping the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 open figure (DD-010) is not bank-verified either way, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. Clause 7.3 of DD-004 conditions transfer of project materials on payment.
- **Incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DL §6):** The Seller calls DD-006 "not expected to be material." The disclosure itself says it is not a confirmed breach and states no loss. The playbook says assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction, and require preservation of logs, investigation and updates. The Seller's "not material" label goes beyond what the record supports and should be rejected. ~1,240 records may be involved, and the investigation is open.
- **Sandbar renewals (DL §8):** The Seller calls AUD 330,000 (3 × AUD 110,000) ordinary-course. The playbook says assess, with no automatic debt classification or price deduction. The disclosure doesn't say whether each is unavoidable, terminable or accrued. We should ask for the contracts and their termination terms before accepting the characterisation.
- **Title (DL §10; cl Title):** The Seller relies on DD-012, the Company share register, as evidence of title. The playbook treats DD-012 as a supplied internal source, not independent proof. We need independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence.
- **Tax/IP (Seller update):** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." The playbook keeps these categories open and separate. They are not settled, and we should assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.

### D. Items not covered by the playbook

- **Office lease (DL §7):** The lease has a notification obligation. The Seller says it isn't a landlord consent requirement. We should ask for the lease clause and confirm in writing.
- **Mossvale (DL §9):** A restriction on assignment exists, but the Seller says it doesn't require consent just because shares are sold. This needs a legal check against the clause text. It isn't a playbook item, so I'd flag it for the deal team rather than assert a position.

## Part 2: What to push back on

**Priority 1 (deal-breakers, to escalate immediately):**
1. Fraud carve-out restored across all limitations, reliance and remedy clauses, with no waiver.
2. Title/capacity moved to a separate regime: 100% cap, six years minimum, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
3. Riverlark payout and security release at Completion; Bluefen consent and condition evidence before Completion.
4. Delete whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure. Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3).

**Priority 2 (economic terms):**
5. Reset general cap to 25% / AUD 6m (not 20%/AUD 4.8m). Do not offer the fallback without Amelia Frost's written approval identifying the draft.
6. Reset de minimis to AUD 5,000 and basket to AUD 50,000, first-dollar.
7. Reset general claims period to 24 months (not 18) without Amelia Frost approval.
8. Add AUD 420,000 bonuses to the funds flow as a specific line item or Seller-funded, including triggered on-costs.

**Priority 3 (specific indemnities and diligence):**
9. Broaden Ironquay indemnity; keep the SOW3 cure; obtain payment confirmation for the AUD 180,000.
10. DD-006: require log preservation, investigation scope, and regular updates. Reject "not material" characterisation and do not accept or assert breach, harm or quantum.
11. Sandbar: obtain contracts and termination terms. No automatic debt or price deduction.
12. Title: independent evidence of ownership, encumbrances and authority, not DD-012 alone.
13. Tax and IP: keep open and separate from the general regime.
14. Lease and Mossvale: confirm the consent/notification position from the clause text.

**Drafting points:** Reject the "any limitation applies to all Claims" default in cl 12.3/13. Each category must stand on its own terms.

## Part 3: Summary of recommendations

The Seller's draft is not a workable base. Its headline terms (20%/AUD 4.8m cap, 18 months, AUD 250k basket, AUD 25k de minimis) are our fallbacks presented as settled, and it drops title into the general regime, removes the fraud carve-out, and uses whole-data-room disclosure with a blanket knowledge bar. The completion mechanics (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses) and specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar, title) also fall short of the playbook.

**Recommended next steps:**
1. Return a full mark-up that reinstates our opening positions: 25%/AUD 6m cap, AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k first-dollar basket, 24 months, separate Title regime (100%, 6+ years), fraud carve-out.
2. Do not offer or concede the 20%/AUD 4.8m cap, the 18-month period, or any other fallback without Amelia Frost's prior written approval identifying the draft.
3. Insist on the completion conditions (Bluefen, Riverlark payout, bonuses in funds flow) before Completion.
4. Delete the whole-data-room disclosure and the cl 8.3 knowledge bar.
5. Request the outstanding diligence items: Bluefen consent, Riverlark payoff letter, bonus on-cost calculation, Ironquay payment evidence, DD-006 investigation updates, Sandbar contracts, independent title evidence, and lease/Mossvale clause text.
6. Keep Tax and IP open and separate, with no unlimited liability and no resolution assumed.
